scope: Read-only comparison of current Intel nine-page draft against published Waterloo 2026 and Yale 2025 competition decks. Josh pitch unavailable. No claim that copying winning features causes winning.

visual_review.layout_finding: Intel is a portrait serif editorial memo; Waterloo is a 16:9 sans-serif evidence deck with numbered thesis bands, section navigation, high-contrast recommendation, exhibit titles and compact source footers. Yale is a 4:3 navy-and-grey deck with side-by-side disagreement and thesis/forecast boxes.

transferable_changes.change: Use landscape 16:9 with white background, dark navy/charcoal text, one red accent and pale grey exhibit fields.
transferable_changes.evidence: Waterloo p3/p35 visual review; Yale p2/p8 visual review.
transferable_changes.boundary: Do not copy logos, school identity, charts, research claims or exact text.

transferable_changes.change: Use one sans-serif family and strong title/body hierarchy; reduce long first-person paragraphs to 2-3 evidence bullets per claim.
transferable_changes.evidence: Waterloo p3 and Yale p8 vs current Intel p1.
transferable_changes.boundary: Retain scope, forecast date and adverse cases; do not use an artificially forceful investment conclusion.

transferable_changes.change: Put relative SHORT, reference quote, dated current value and conditional 2030 position return on a compact first-page dashboard.
transferable_changes.evidence: Waterloo p1/p3 and Yale p1 make direction, current price and target immediately visible.
transferable_changes.boundary: $46.96 is Dec.31 2026 conditional value, not a 2030 cover target or guaranteed downside; central 2030 Intel value is $70.98.

transferable_changes.change: Use two numbered thesis rows with specific mechanisms and one forecast implication each.
transferable_changes.boundary: These are two linked judgments in one conditional thesis, not independent proven alpha sources.

transferable_changes.change: Keep a simple footer section navigation and repeat thesis numbering beside the relevant valuation inputs.
transferable_changes.boundary: Keep within the M37 maximum ten PDF pages, rather than borrowing long appendices.

transferable_changes.change: Give exhibits most of each page and convert prose into observed evidence / forecast treatment / what would falsify it columns.
transferable_changes.boundary: A scenario comparison is not a measured disagreement with consensus.

transferable_changes.change: Use assertive but accurate finding headlines: operating profit recovers before owner cash; qualified capacity still requires funding; premium mix does not establish permanent margins.
transferable_changes.evidence: Waterloo claim-led summaries and charts; current Intel p3-p5 support these narrower claims.
transferable_changes.boundary: Do not rename owner cash as GAAP free cash flow, distributions or shareholder returns.

transferable_changes.change: Add one compact path from 2027 funding/output through 2028 cash conversion to 2029-30 durable economics.
transferable_changes.boundary: These are observation windows, not verified future event dates or guaranteed repricing catalysts.

transferable_changes.change: Move lengthy accounting explanations to one methods/source page while keeping short material qualifications adjacent to each chart.
transferable_changes.evidence: Winner decks use exhibits with brief sources and larger supporting appendices.
transferable_changes.boundary: Do not bury that central future value rises, the hedge is conditional, or alternative ERP assumptions erase its advantage.

transferable_changes.change: Use a two-column risk / evidence-that-would-change-the-view panel instead of repeated prose caveats.
transferable_changes.evidence: Yale p25 risks/mitigants; current Intel p7 already supplies numerical checkpoints.
transferable_changes.boundary: Risks are real opposing outcomes; do not present every one as solved.

content_gaps.examples: Waterloo p35: 170K vs 186K locations and 39% vs 43% GM for 2029E. Yale p8/p21: thesis-specific revenue/EBITDA deltas versus 2028 consensus.
content_gaps.intel: Current p6 compares EPS proxies to one analyst while acknowledging accounting differences; no matched consensus cash-flow or mature-margin error has been established.
content_gaps.action_now: Add a clearly labeled bull-case/own-case/evidence/forecast comparison using existing inputs.
content_gaps.remaining: A matched, sourced expectations benchmark and evidence supporting why ours should be right.

content_gaps.item: Original customer, channel or expert evidence
content_gaps.examples: Waterloo p2 reports 13 expert calls, 188 customer interviews and 21,611 scraped datapoints.
content_gaps.intel: Primary company/supplier public disclosures and our calculations; no interviews or surveys performed.
content_gaps.remaining: Original research if useful and methodologically defensible; counts alone are not an edge.

content_gaps.examples: Yale p8 assigns each thesis to revenue, EBITDA, multiple and share-count differences.
content_gaps.intel: Mechanisms and financial outputs appear on separate pages, but linkage is less easy to scan.
content_gaps.action_now: Add rows mapping funded capacity to capex/WC and mix durability to ASP/mature DCAI margin/capital productivity.
content_gaps.remaining: Do not attribute a total value delta to one variable when multiple assumptions move.

content_gaps.intel: Current p7 numerical annual checkpoints but no timeline.
content_gaps.action_now: Turn existing annual checkpoints into observation windows.
content_gaps.remaining: No proven near-term repricing catalyst; competition does not require one.

content_gaps.item: Historical operating baseline and competitive overview
content_gaps.examples: Yale p3-p6 segment revenue, industry share, history, leverage and FCF; Waterloo p4-p6 transaction economics/segments.
content_gaps.intel: Current p2 explains business, eliminations and prospective market-unit logic; historical margins/ASP appear selectively elsewhere.
content_gaps.action_now: Compact baseline panel if verified actual figures fit; do not add a whole generic industry page.
content_gaps.remaining: Matched actual-to-forecast comparisons help calibration; current model scopes differ from reported consolidated revenue.

content_gaps.examples: Waterloo p32 relative value; Yale p22/p23 SOTP, precedent transactions and comparables.
content_gaps.intel: APV and operating/risk sensitivities plus a rough EPS multiple; no fully reconciled peer valuation.
content_gaps.action_now: Keep the limitation explicit; only add a crosscheck if scopes can be reconciled.
content_gaps.remaining: Intel integrated foundry/product structure makes indiscriminate fabless peer multiples unreliable.

already_present: Position capital, return and borrow assumptions
editorial_caution: Published winning decks contain draft artifacts or inconsistencies too: Yale p25 has an xx% placeholder and Waterloo p33 versus p34/p35 differs on the displayed GM. Emulate hierarchy and evidence structure, not every source detail or level of rhetorical confidence.
recommendation: Make the deck look and read like an investment presentation now; distinguish newly improved presentation from unresolved investment edge. The missing matched expectations evidence cannot be manufactured through wording.
